question: Immunology researchers attempt to characterize the role of several cytokines in a 5-year-old male’s allergic reaction to peanuts. Months after initial exposure to peanuts, the child was brought to the ER due to repeat exposure with symptoms of anaphylaxis that resolved following epinephrine injection and supportive therapy. Which of the following best describes the role of IL-4 in the child’s response:?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: IL-4 -> B cell class switching -> 80% CHAIN: IL-4 -> Stimulates IgA production -> 70% CHAIN: IL-4 -> Macrophage activation -> Th2 cell differentiation -> 80%
enhanced_information: IL-4 is primarily involved in B cell class switching and Th2 cell differentiation, leading to the production of IgA. This aligns with the consensus that IL-4 plays a key role in promoting antibody class switching to IgE and IgG1 in allergic responses.
analysis: IL-4 is known to play a crucial role in B cell class switching, particularly promoting the production of IgE antibodies, which are central to allergic reactions like anaphylaxis.
